description: Per-shot pixel tolerances for parity specs, measured as run-to-run noise of the live oracle (same Mac, Chromium build in capture-meta.json). Canvas PNGs and shot JSON (gl draw calls/triangles, html, cssHash, storage) were exact in every run: tolerance 0. Only DOM-overlay PNGs show noise.

runs.liveVsLive: capture-live-baselines.mjs --verify (fresh capture vs committed live baselines)

policy.rule: shot tolerance = max observed ratio x2, rounded up to 1e-4; shots not listed use 0

nonDeterministic.desktop-chromium/playthrough--after-ques: tower-label world label hangs off the right viewport edge (x~1313/1280); Chrome rasterizes the clipped layer differently run to run (~0.13%).
nonDeterministic.desktop-chromium/playthrough--quest-comp: same off-edge tower-label, under the dialog backdrop blur (~0.05%).
nonDeterministic.desktop-chromium/bridge-6--play.dom.png: 20 px on an off-edge world label (0.002%).
nonDeterministic.desktop-chromium/menus--map-open.dom.png: 3 px, map overlay map-in keyframe animation on a composited layer (oracle run only).
nonDeterministic.mobile-pixel/playthrough--quiz-correct-3: 3 px, dialog pop/reward-pop keyframe animation on a composited layer.

recommendation: Keep pixel gating for canvas shots (exact) and for DOM shots at tolerance 0. For the listed shots, do not raise global tolerance: either mask the off-screen world labels (#tower-label, #city-label when their translate x exceeds the viewport) in DOM shots, or gate them structurally via the shot JSON (html + cssHash + gl calls/triangles are exact) and the oracle scene JSON. Structural gating is preferred because it is exact and catches label text/position regressions that a mask would hide.
